lines.text: Many learners say: I am afraid from dogs.
Better: I am afraid of dogs.
Say afraid of, not afraid from.
Of! She is afraid of the dark.

data.why: Say afraid of, not afraid from.

native.tip: في العربية نقول «خائف من»، أما في الإنجليزية فنقول afraid of: “I am afraid of dogs.” وليس “I am afraid from dogs.”
native.caption: هل تقول أحيانًا هذه الجملة؟ “I am afraid from dogs” 😅 بعد afraid نستخدم of وليس from، فالجملة الصحيحة “I am afraid of dogs.” استمع إلى Carlos وكرّر! تدرّب أكثر في تطبيق Lexkite.
native.comment: الإجابة: “of” — بعد afraid نستخدم of وليس from. اختبار مجاني هنا: {link}

en.tip: After afraid we use of, not from: “I am afraid of dogs.” not “I am afraid from dogs.”
en.caption: Do you sometimes say this? “I am afraid from dogs” 😅 After afraid we use of, not from, so the right sentence is “I am afraid of dogs.” Listen to Carlos and repeat! Practice more in the Lexkite app.
